messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: latency_slo.p95 breached for /streaming/generate in prod - region us-west-2. p95=2.9s (SLO=1.2s), p99=9.8s. Error spikes on streaming tails. Paging eng-oncall.
maya: saw the page, I'm on it. glancing at grafana: https://grafana.internal/alerts/4627 - looks like a step up ~09:12 UTC, tail latency spikes across several shards.
samir: which stack? runtime or prefill? my quick read from traces shows lots of streaming stalls at decode step, and a flood of prefill evictions.
maya: exactly - kv cache free ratio dropped from 42% -> 8% between 09:10-09:14. lots of eviction churn. I can see eviction logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:23Z WARN kv_cache: evict slab_id=7 freed=12 prefill_hits=0 decode_hits=18
2026-03-15T09:12:24Z WARN kv_cache: eviction_queue.len=1023 prefill_inflight=240 decode_inflight=18
```
nirav: wow prefill_inflight >> decode_inflight. that mismatch can fragment slabs and increase tail latency for streaming clients that rely on cached KV.
tessa: think the recent change to prefill concurrency ramp (deploy yesterday) increased prefill parallelism. maybe it oversubscribed cache.
maya: rolling back prefill concurrency is one mitigation. but we need an immediate low-risk action: 1) enable eviction-throttle to cap evictions 2) bump slab reclaim threshold 3) route streaming to best-effort fallback pool for affected customers.
samir: on the routing: I can flip the routing policy to route streaming requests >128 tokens to fallback-compat model in us-west-2. That should reduce pressure on hot shards. running command now:
```
# route-change
redwoodctl routing set --route "/streaming" --predicate "tokens>128 and region==us-west-2" --target fallback-compat-v1 --dry-run=false
```
samir: done. live: some requests are now landing on fallback-compat-v1. ops-bot: reroute event posted: https://ops.internal/events/rv-784
ops-bot: REROUTE: /streaming -> fallback-compat-v1 for tokens>128 (triggered by samir)
maya: I'm toggling eviction-throttle to 100 evictions/sec on shard group A to slow churn.
```
redwoodctl cache set --group shard-A --eviction-throttle 100
```
maya: throttle applied.
nirav: also increasing slab_reserve from 64MB -> 96MB for shard-A to reduce fragmentation. applying now.
```
redwoodctl cache set --group shard-A --slab_reserve 96MB
```
nirav: applied. monitoring cache_free_ratio and decode latency.
tessa: I'll coordinate handoff notes. short customer impact check: which customers saw streaming stalls? queries to prometheus show three high-traffic tenants with p99 > 12s: tenant-alpha, tenant-b, small-saas-co.
maya: sending customer pings to success: "we're aware and mitigating, will update in 30m". @sre-manager do we need to open a P1 incident page?
sre-manager: yes open P1 given SLO breach and multiple paying tenants impacted. start an incident page and add runbook link.
maya: opening incident page: https://incidents.internal/4627182345 - added initial triage notes and mitigation actions.

samir: after reroute and throttle, p95 dropped to 1.5s at 09:20 UTC and p99 to 4.2s. still above SLO but improving. streaming stall rate cut ~70%.
ops-bot: METRICS: p95=1.5s p99=4.2s prefill_inflight=62 decode_inflight=40 cache_free=18%
nirav: looks like eviction churn slowed, but cache_free still low. we should run a targeted prefill backoff: cap prefill_concurrency to 16 per node.
maya: doing a soft rollout of prefill backoff via config flag for us-west-2:
```
redwoodctl feature set --flag prefill_concurrency --value 16 --scope us-west-2 --rollout 20%
```
maya: rollout started at 09:24 UTC.
tessa: doc note: add to postmortem that yesterday's prefill parallelism increase was root-contrib. also record that slabs fragmented when prefill >> decode.
samir: telemetry: I pushed a temporary log marker to better capture prefill vs decode hits per-kv-key for deeper debug:
```
logger.info("kv_prefill_decode_snapshot", {"prefill": X, "decode": Y, "key_shard": Z})
```
maya: we should also consider short-term customer-facing mitigation: enable streaming timeouts to drop stalled streams at 8s and return partial results rather than blocking.
sre-manager: approve. implement on gateway layer with a 30-minute TTL. samir can you flip?
samir: setting gateway streaming timeout 8s for affected route.
```
redwoodctl gateway set-timeout --route /streaming --timeout 8s --scope us-west-2
```
samir: applied. initial customer error rates increased slightly (clients now get partial responses) but user-perceived latency improved for many.

nirav: summary so far: actions taken: reroute long streams to fallback-compat, eviction-throttle on shard-A, slab_reserve bump, prefill_concurrency roll out (20%), gateway timeout 8s. outcome: p95 -> 1.1s, p99 -> 2.9s by 09:33 UTC. still monitoring.
maya: agree. next: continue rollout of prefill backoff to 100% if metrics keep improving. schedule a controlled rollback of yesterday's prefill parallelism change in deploy board.
tessa: I'm compiling a quick customer-impact blurb for success and cs, will send once we hit stable window (30m of p95 under 1.2s).

sre-manager: handoff plan: Maya will keep monitoring for another 30m, then hand over to Nirav for night shift. If p99 < 3s and eviction rate < 50/s, mark as mitigated and start postmortem. otherwise escalate to infra release lead.
maya: ack. adding notes to incident page and leaving runbook pointer and commands executed.
maya: final note during handoff: commands to revert routing and timeout are in incident page. if rollback needed: reverse routing then restore gateway timeouts and prefill flags.

oncall-bot: AUTO-HANDOFF scheduled: maya -> nirav at 09:55 UTC
nirav: taking over at 09:55 UTC if still needed. thanks team.
maya: thanks everyone. will update status in 20m. :thumbsup:
